title: Grafana Assistant Expands to More Than 30 Data Sources
gist: Grafana Labs expanded Grafana Assistant to query and correlate data across 30+ sources via natural language, part of a broader 2026 push (AI Observability, MCP support, self-managed availability) as observability vendors shift from competing on telemetry collection to competing on AI-driven investigation capabilities.

insights.claim: Grafana Labs expanded Grafana Assistant to query and correlate data across more than 30 different data sources through natural language, letting operators, developers, and SREs investigate incidents and troubleshoot without switching between multiple monitoring tools.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Reduces tool-switching friction in incident response, a direct competitive lever against Datadog, Dynatrace, Splunk, and New Relic in the observability market.
insights.quote: Grafana Assistant, enabling its AI-powered observability assistant to query and correlate data across more than 30 different data sources through natural language
insights.locator: Grafana Labs has expanded the capabilities

insights.claim: The latest Grafana Assistant release adds support for enterprise data sources including Snowflake, Oracle, Elasticsearch, Dynatrace, Honeycomb, MongoDB, Zabbix, and Jira, allowing investigations to blend operational, infrastructure, and business context in a single conversation.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Grafana is reaching beyond pure observability data into business systems (Snowflake, Jira), signaling ambition to be a general incident-context layer, not just a metrics dashboard.
insights.quote: support has expanded to include additional enterprise data sources such as Snowflake, Oracle, Elasticsearch, Dynatrace, Honeycomb, MongoDB, Zabbix, and Jira
insights.locator: With the latest release, support has expanded

insights.claim: Grafana is marketing the multi-source expansion as a step toward "unified observability," positioning the assistant as a way to eliminate fragmented operational data spread across dozens of disconnected platforms.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: "Unified observability" is becoming the industry framing for AI-in-ops products; watch whether Grafana can back this claim with real cross-source correlation accuracy versus marketing.
insights.locator: The company claims that this update is a step toward

insights.claim: Grafana Assistant translates natural language into query languages like PromQL, LogQL, SQL, and TraceQL on the user's behalf while respecting existing permissions and role-based access controls, rather than requiring engineers to learn each query language.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Preserving RBAC while auto-generating queries is a key enterprise-adoption gate for AI copilots touching sensitive telemetry and business data.
insights.quote: the assistant translates natural language into the appropriate queries while respecting existing permissions and role-based access controls
insights.locator: Rather than forcing users to learn multiple query languages

insights.claim: The data-source expansion builds on an AI strategy Grafana unveiled at GrafanaCON 2026, where the company positioned AI as an operational partner rather than simply a chatbot.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Signals Grafana's product positioning is shifting from dashboards/alerting toward autonomous or semi-autonomous operational agents, a category investors should track for margin and retention impact.
insights.quote: the company positioned AI as an operational partner rather than simply a chatbot
insights.locator: The enhancement builds on Grafana Assistant's broader AI strategy

insights.claim: Throughout 2026 Grafana has steadily expanded its AI portfolio beyond the Assistant itself, introducing AI Observability for monitoring large language model applications, Model Context Protocol (MCP) support for integrating external AI agents, and making Grafana Assistant available to self-managed Grafana Enterprise and OSS deployments.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: MCP support and self-managed availability widen Grafana's addressable base beyond cloud-hosted customers, and LLM-app monitoring positions Grafana to capture spend from the AI-application boom itself.
insights.quote: introducing AI Observability for monitoring large language model applications, Model Context Protocol (MCP) support for integrating external AI agents, and making Grafana Assistant available to self-managed Grafana Enterprise and OSS deployments
insights.locator: As a result, like its competitors, Grafana has steadily expanded

insights.claim: Observability vendors are increasingly competing on AI investigation capabilities rather than on telemetry collection alone: Datadog's Bits AI performs automated investigations and root cause analysis, Dynatrace's Davis AI combines causal reasoning with automation, Splunk integrates an AI Assistant into security and observability workflows, and New Relic's Intelligent Observability automatically correlates telemetry and recommends remediation.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: The observability market's competitive axis has shifted to AI-driven root-cause/remediation features; vendor differentiation and pricing power will increasingly hinge on model quality and data-source breadth rather than raw ingestion volume.
insights.quote: observability vendors increasingly compete on AI capabilities rather than telemetry collection alone
insights.locator: Grafana's announcement comes as observability vendors

insights.claim: As distributed systems grow more complex and AI-powered applications generate increasing volumes of telemetry, simply collecting data is no longer enough, driving demand for intelligent systems that correlate logs, metrics, traces, profiles, infrastructure events, and application behavior.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: AI application growth is itself a demand driver for observability tooling upgrades, creating a secondary market tailwind for vendors like Grafana, Datadog, and Dynatrace beyond traditional infrastructure monitoring.
insights.quote: simply collecting data is no longer enough
insights.locator: The announcement reflects broader shifts occurring within observability itself

insights.claim: The accuracy and usefulness of Grafana Assistant's natural-language investigations remain dependent on the completeness of underlying telemetry, correct access permissions, and the reliability of AI models in generating and executing queries across diverse, heterogeneous data sources.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: A key risk flag for buyers: cross-source AI correlation is only as good as data completeness and model reliability, so pilot results may vary widely by customer's existing telemetry hygiene.
insights.quote: the quality and accuracy of an assistant's responses remain dependent on several factors, including the completeness of the underlying telemetry, appropriate access permissions, and the ability of AI models to reliably generate and execute queries across diverse and heterogeneous data sources
insights.locator: While natural-language interfaces can make investigations faster
